config.preparation: Create timestamp = dteday + hr as a datetime. Create label_end = timestamp + 1h and prev_timestamp = timestamp - 1h. Validate that timestamp is unique; if duplicates exist, flag them rather than silently joining. Self-join the table to itself as current c and previous p on p.timestamp = c.prev_timestamp to obtain previous-hour weather columns weathersit_prev, temp_prev, atemp_prev, hum_prev, and windspeed_prev. Validate cardinality by confirming the join does not fan out: the number of joined rows should equal the number of current rows and no current row should have more than one previous match. Keep NaN when no previous hour exists. Create is_commuter_focus = 1 when workingday == 1 and hr is in {7, 8, 9, 16, 17, 18, 19}, else 0. Use cnt as the target. Exclude instant, dteday, timestamp, label_end, prev_timestamp, current weathersit, current temp, current atemp, current hum, current windspeed, casual, registered, and cnt from features. Fit imputation and scaling on the training portion only, with median imputation for absent previous-hour weather.
config.rationale: The objective is to predict a continuous hourly rental count from information available at the start of the hour, so this is a regression task. A temporal holdout on timestamp matches the operational setting and, with label_end = timestamp + 1h, purges training rows whose outcomes are not yet observable at the validation boundary. Features are limited to known calendar variables and previous-hour weather, avoiding current-hour weather, target components, target lags, and full-data learned transforms. Standard preprocessing is appropriate for the small numeric/categorical feature set and will impute absent previous-hour weather using training-only medians. Random Forest, LightGBM, and XGBoost are the allowed CPU models; run them with registry defaults (100 trees and at most 4 threads) as three of the five allowed trials, stopping early if validation RMSE plateaus. Overall RMSE is the requested selection metric, and the is_commuter_focus flag encodes the user's high-priority working-day peak hours while diagnostics can separately inspect those hours.
